mentions.name: Cloud lab that doesn't suck
mentions.description: This project aims to build a cloud lab—a remote lab that is actually useful for people. The author outlines automation ideas for it: a robot dedicated to loading and running 48–96 lane gel boxes once or twice a day with batched samples, keeping qPCR machines full to make them cheap, using plate readers and bulk reagents (sourced cheaply from China) for quantification, and aggregating equipment needs so shaking incubators become cheap despite scarce used cytomat parts for shaking.
mentions.problem: Existing remote 'cloud labs' aren't actually useful for the people who would use them.
mentions.source_excerpt: My main goal is to create a cloud lab that doesn't suck - ie, a remote lab that is actually useful for people
